subject: Post-call: SDK demo & minimal local setup for tool-calling + embeddings
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Nov 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SDK demo & minimal local setup for tool-calling + embeddings

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get your engineers into a local validation loop this week.

Recap (very short)
- Goal: validate an in-house proof-of-concept using Redwood SDK (Python or TS) to: 1) call models with structured output & tool-calling, 2) evaluate embeddings + a small reranker, 3) run locally inside your dev VPC before moving to Dedicated.
- Constraints you mentioned: on-prem compliance for sensitive PII, prefer EU-region models for EU data but initial testing can run in our us-west sandbox, and your SRE will validate network egress policy.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) I’m attaching a lightweight quickstart bundle (redwood-sdk-quickstart-stubs.zip) with a Python and TS sample app, a Docker dev compose, and a minimal prompt set for embedding/rerank smoke tests.
2) Camila will follow up with exact env vars and a short walkthrough (10–15m) of: API key scopes, routing to a cost-optimized variant, and enabling tool calling stubs.
3) Please confirm preferred time windows for a 30-min hands-on lab (timezone PST/CEST). Ideally within next 48 hours so your SRE can run the local network checks.

Quick local validation checklist (what your engineer can run locally)
- Clone repo (link below), set REDWOOD_API_KEY (read-only/test key we’ll issue), set REDWOOD_REGION=us-west or eu-central for your later tests.
- Python quick test: python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python examples/python/tool_call_demo.py --local
- TS quick test: npm ci && npm run dev:local && curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
- Embeddings smoke: scripts/run_embeddings_smoke.sh will index 500 sample docs and run a top-5 rerank comparison between a cosine baseline and Redwood reranker.

I’ll wait for preferred lab slots and will assign a short-lived test API key once times are fixed.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart-stubs.zip, integration-playbook-summary.pdf

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

1) Our SRE prefers we run an air-gapped test in a dev subnet with NAT egress via a proxy. Is the quickstart able to run with an outbound-only proxy (we can provide the proxy host/port)?
2) For embeddings: we’ll be testing on ~25k small docs (customer tickets). Any recommended memory/quantization profile for the reranker in the quickstart? We don’t need full production perf, just a representative throughput estimate.

Available lab windows (PST): Nov 9 between 09:00–12:00 or Nov 10 between 13:00–16:00. Priya (cc) will join from our infra team.

Hi Alex / Priya — jumping in with the technical details you asked for. Short answers first:

- Proxy support: yes — both Python and TS samples accept HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars. The included docker-compose.override.yml shows how to set a proxy for containerized runs. We’ll also provide a test token restricted to the sandbox org so you don’t need open access.
- Embeddings + reranker profile for ~25k docs (smoke): start with FP16 quantized encoder, 16GB GPU-like memory in our Dedicated sim will roughly mirror the CPU-bottlenecked local run. For local smoke, the script uses faiss.Flat + batching=256; you should see a baseline index + rerank pass in ~6–12 minutes (depends on machine I/O).

Snippets and links
- GitHub quickstart (forkable): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/tree/quickstart/integrata-playground
- Minimal env (examples/.env.sample)
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_test_xxx
  REDWOOD_REGION=us-west
  REDWOOD_PROXY=http://proxy.internal:3128
  REDWOOD_ROUTING_POLICY=cost_preferred

- Docker: docker-compose up --build will spin up a tiny express proxy and the sample app; to mimic NAT egress set the proxy container host:port in your dev subnet.

Tool-calling notes
- The tool stubs in examples/python/tools/ implement a local HTTP tool endpoint that accepts structured JSON and returns deterministic responses; that’s sufficient to validate the tool-calling handshake and structured-output schema.

What I’ll bring to the lab
- Short walkthrough (10m) of the sample app flows, 10m for embedding/rerank run, 10m for interpreting latency/cost counters in the logs.

I’ve attached the quickstart bundle Jonas mentioned (same filenames). If you’d like, Karthik and I can add a small on-prem toggle to demonstrate VPC-mirroring (no external traffic) but that will add ~1–2 hours prep — can do if you want the deeper demo during the lab.

—
Camila Reyes
